state.context: I32 fixes every route handler at callable http::server_response (http::request) emits []. Mandatory per-function assertions collide with this shape: measured runs fail all handler rows as outcome mismatches since fresh response tokens never satisfy the runner's identity-plus-deep-equality rule. The C comparison rules omit opaque values, and the P10 sink contract exposes no response readers, so Can cannot inspect what a handler returned. Fixture-path records still attest the handler's boundary calls and arguments, and staged loopback checks still read true wire behavior. P13 wants supplied-completion callback assertions, and established HTML suites assert only failures and void rather than opaque successes.

opaque.instructions: Select the assertion design that stays truthful about opaque handler results.

criteria.bare_opaque_ok: Permit value-free ok solely in assertion expectations for excluded opaque results, with the runner accepting undefined expectations against opaque outcomes. Fixture layout, argument checks, and completion kinds stay verified in Can; response bytes stay verified in loopback.
criteria.exempt_handlers: Drop mandatory assertions for mounted-handler-shaped functions via explicit correction, leaving loopback as the single execution witness and Can assertions to models, mounts, and constructors.
criteria.vacuous_runner: Accept every opaque-ok versus opaque-ok match in the runner, taking the C exclusion as a blanket comparison waiver.
criteria.structural_response_compare: Preserve valued expectations by structurally equating statuses, headers, and bodies from private response storage.
